newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croats think they're poorer than ever - survey.
newsitem.headline: Croats think they're poorer than ever - survey.

text.p: More than two-thirds of Croatians think they are poorer than before independence and half do not believe the government can make things better, according to an opinion poll published on Monday.
The daily Slobodna Dalmacija published the poll, carried out by the independent Metronom poll agency which made a telephone survey of 300 people across Croatia.
Some 68.3 percent described their standard of living as poor and 48.7 percent thought that the government was incapable of bringing about a recovery.
Nearly half said their situation has worsened since Croatia gained independence from former Yugoslavia in 1991 and fought a war with its Serb minority.
Croatia launched an austerity programme that slashed inflation but impoverished many of its citizens.
Only 2.7 percent of those polled thought workers could win improvements by striking.
Since last week Croatia has seen the largest wave of popular protest in years, as public workers and railmen staged strikes over poor wages.
